segments.text: Okay, now, how are you both getting on with the assignment?
Well, to be honest, I'm getting a bit muddled up.
I've done loads of reading and taken notes, but I'm still confused about what to include.
It's only a 3,000-word essay, isn't it?
Yes, it is, but it's worth 50% of the module marks,
so you need to get good marks for this in case you don't do so well in the exam.
Have you identified the main points you want to include?
Well, no, not really. That's what I'm having trouble with.
I thought that if I did lots of reading and took good notes,
it would be easy to write, but I'm still confused.
Did you analyse the question before you started reading?
You know, to make sure you really understood it, and then make a plan.
Er, not exactly. No-one's ever shown me how to do that before.
I'm not sure what you mean.
No, me neither. I'm having trouble too.
It sounds like you two need to do a course in study skills, especially academic writing.
Oh, Sarah, do you remember that guy I was telling you about who had done a course in
writing skills. He says that his marks have improved a lot since then, so maybe we need
to get ourselves enrolled as soon as possible. I think he said he went for just two hours
a week for a term and it really helped.
Well, I definitely recommend that you do that. You might surprise yourself and realise
you do have some of the skills already, but I'm sure there will also be things you can
learn. Think of it as an investment. Time spent now will hopefully make your studies
here easier and more successful. Now, let's get back to this essay. James, can you help
Sarah out by outlining all the main points that need to go into the essay?
I'll have a go. I think that after the introduction, we need to describe what happened in the
past, you know, give the background. Can I interrupt you there James? What is the
main part of the question you are being asked in the title? I mean, what words
exactly are used? Evaluate the reasons why the phenomenon has reappeared and
assess the implications for future practice. Yes, so what does that mean?
What are you being asked to do?
Erm...
Sarah?
Erm...
Well, are you being asked to describe anything?
I don't think so.
I suppose not.
So, do you think it's necessary to write about the past, give background in the main section?
No. But I thought you always had to put things into a context.
Well, that's right, you do, but in this essay you can do that briefly in the introduction
and not waste too many words by putting it in the main body.
Are you going to offer a definition of the concept?
Yes, I learned at school that you should do that, but for my reading I've seen different
definitions, so which one am I supposed to use?
Which one are you using, James?
one I understand best. Holmes, 2007, is the one I'm using.
That's fine, James, but make sure you acknowledge that there are several definitions available.
Just make it clear which one you are using for the purpose of this essay. I really do
think that you two would benefit enormously from a course in academic writing skills.
It would cover all the issues you are having trouble with. Go along to the Centre for
English language and academic skills after you've left me and enrol on a course, they're
really helpful in there and they know exactly what you need to write more successfully.
Now let's get back to those main points.
